newsitem.title: USA: COMEX copper barely changed early as Inco strikes.
newsitem.headline: COMEX copper barely changed early as Inco strikes.

text.p: COMEX copper was barely changed in quiet early trade as the strike at Inco's Sudbury operations gave the market modest support at best, dealers said.
News that Sudbury workers were on strike helped boost LME copper overnight, but there was little sign of significant follow through on COMEX at the opening.
Inco produces 90,700 tonnes of copper a year and fears of a strike prompted higher spot premiums in the U.S. Northeast market, merchants said last week.
"The market still looks a little toppy and there is still more selling around after yesterday," a broker said. "Inco on its own is not enough to give strength to go back up."
At 0919 EDT, July COMEX was up 0.05 cent at 117.20 cents a lb, traded 117.40 to 116.15 cents. Spot June was flat at 117.00 cents.

Copper prices fell Monday as the market corrected after the recent sharp run-up. Technical indicators have slid from overbought territory, with nine-day RSI at 55 percent and 14-day RSI at 60 percent, both down from more than 70 percent last week.
LME stocks fell a nominal 525 tonnes to 132,500 tonnes Tuesday as the trend of more modest changes in stock levels continued.
